description: A single-panel figure that is a rendered table — Table 8, "A comparison among the hardening effects in 9Al-xMn-1C at 600 °C and 800 °C tempering." There are no axes, curves, micrographs or scale bars; the whole information content is tabulated text and numbers. The left column is headed "Composition (wt%)" and the right block is headed "Hardness [HV]", subdivided into three data columns whose headers are printed run together as "Hot-rolled600 °C — Tempered800 °C — Tempered", i.e. the hot-rolled state, 600 °C tempering and 800 °C tempering. Three alloy rows are given: 9Al-10Mn-1C (273, 439, 356 HV), 9Al-20Mn-1C (233, 359, 249 HV) and 9Al-30Mn-1C (216, 330, 238 HV). The table demonstrates that hot-rolled hardness falls monotonically as Mn increases from 10 to 30 wt% (273 → 233 → 216 HV); that 600 °C tempering produces a strong hardening peak in every composition, highest at 9Al-10Mn-1C (439 HV); and that 800 °C tempering leaves intermediate hardness (356, 249, 238 HV). The ranking by Mn content is preserved after both tempering treatments, while the hardening increment relative to the hot-rolled state shrinks as Mn rises. It is a composite-free, single-table figure.

observations.observation: The figure is a table (Table 8), not a plot: its columns are 'Composition (wt%)' and 'Hardness [HV]' with three data columns for hot-rolled, 600 °C — Tempered and 800 °C — Tempered states.
The table lists exactly three alloy compositions: 9Al-10Mn-1C, 9Al-20Mn-1C and 9Al-30Mn-1C.
Hardness values for 9Al-10Mn-1C are 273 HV hot-rolled, 439 HV after 600 °C tempering and 356 HV after 800 °C tempering.
Hardness values for 9Al-20Mn-1C are 233 HV hot-rolled, 359 HV after 600 °C tempering and 249 HV after 800 °C tempering.
Hardness values for 9Al-30Mn-1C are 216 HV hot-rolled, 330 HV after 600 °C tempering and 238 HV after 800 °C tempering.
Hot-rolled hardness decreases monotonically with increasing Mn content: 273 → 233 → 216 HV for 10, 20 and 30 wt% Mn.
For every composition the 600 °C tempering column holds the maximum hardness (439, 359 and 330 HV), exceeding both the hot-rolled and the 800 °C tempered values.
The 800 °C tempered hardness values lie between the hot-rolled and 600 °C tempered values in all three rows, so the hardening peak is erased but not fully reversed at 800 °C.

The hardness increment produced by 600 °C tempering relative to the hot-rolled state is largest for 9Al-10Mn-1C (273 → 439 HV) and smallest for 9Al-30Mn-1C (216 → 330 HV), i.e. the hardening response weakens as Mn content rises.
The highest single value printed is 439 HV (9Al-10Mn-1C, 600 °C tempered) and the lowest is 216 HV (9Al-30Mn-1C, hot-rolled).
The table caption states that it is a comparison among the hardening effects in 9Al-xMn-1C at 600 °C and 800 °C tempering.
Hardness is reported in HV (Vickers hardness); no error bars, standard deviations or number of measurements are given in the table.
